unit: One fixed DNA query/target pair, one fixed alignment mode (NW, SHW or HW), and EDLIB_TASK_PATH, executed through the retained edlib-aligner with one query per invocation, as a path run (EDLIB_TASK_PATH) and as a location-only run (EDLIB_TASK_LOC) of the same executable. Repeated measurements of that same pair/mode are replicates, not separate workloads. The performance suite contains all combinations of nominal aligned-core lengths 10000 and 30000, nominal similarity strata 60%, 70%, 80%, 90% and 99%, and the three modes, with one public and one independently seeded held-out pair per combination: 30 public plus 30 held-out workloads. Train uses the complete public suite; final freshly measures the complete public-plus-held-out suite. Additional short and API-contract cases are mandatory correctness gates, not performance workloads.

metrics.name: cpu_time_seconds
metrics.means: For implementation X and workload w, T_X(w) = min_i P_X,i(w) - min_i L_X,i(w): the smallest of fifteen verifier-measured elapsed durations of fresh path runs (-m MODE -p -f CIG_EXT -r 1 -k -1) minus the smallest of fifteen verifier-measured elapsed durations of fresh location-only runs (-m MODE -l -r 1 -k -1) of the same executable on the same input. The two command lines execute identical work up to the reconstruction call: exec, dynamic loading, the stage-2 guard constructor, FASTA loading, the retained distance search and, in HW mode, the retained start-location search. Only the path run then calls obtainAlignment, converts the path with edlibAlignmentToCigar and prints it. The difference therefore removes start-up, input, the retained search and the effect of the build's code placement on that retained code (measured: two builds of one reconstruction that differ by about 5% in location-only time agree in the difference). Every one of the 60 timed executions of a workload (fifteen rounds; in each round a path run of each lane, then a location-only run of each lane, lane order alternating by round) is validated before its duration is accepted: complete output matched byte for byte against the retained CLI's format for that mode; path runs: printed distance equal to the reference API distance (itself cross-checked against the distance-only engine) and the printed extended CIGAR replayed on the reference's target interval at a cost equal to that distance; location-only runs: printed distance and the complete printed list of (start, end) locations equal to the reference API location result. Each duration is the elapsed wall time of the whole process as measured by the verifier, not by the program: CLOCK_MONOTONIC is read by trusted verifier code in the forked child after CPU pinning, resource limits and the guard are installed, immediately before exec, and again by a verifier thread blocked in wait4 the moment the kernel reports the process reaped. The CLI's own 'Cpu time of searching' line is a diagnostic only in both modes: it must be present, well formed, positive and no greater than the verifier-measured elapsed time of the same run, otherwise the evaluation is invalid, and it never enters the comparison or the score. The subtraction is meaningful only if nothing of a submission executes in the location-only mode, where the reconstruction is never called. That is enforced, not assumed: (1) evaluator.py::body_stays_in_function reads the submitted body as C++ tokens and rejects any body that closes its function (so nothing can be added at namespace scope), refusing line splices, trigraphs and raw string literals instead of interpreting them; (2) elf_surface.py::require_same_launch_surface compares the built candidate executable with the reference executable of the same tree and rejects any difference in the sizes of .preinit_array, .init_array, .fini_array, .init, .fini, .ctors and .dtors, any GNU indirect function or IRELATIVE relocation, any difference in the set of strong global definitions, and any new definition (strong or weak) of a C-level symbol or of a global operator new/delete. The same comparison is applied to the instrumented executables. Candidate and reference use identical inputs, flags, builds, CPU affinity, fixed environment and guard. This is one duration per workload, never an aggregate across pairs or modes. The cpu_time_seconds identifier is retained for compatibility; the value is a difference of verifier-measured elapsed process times, including scheduling wait. No batching, caching or retry-to-pass is introduced; the only sample selection is the minimum of each mode. The minimum is used because the noise of this single-threaded deterministic program is predominantly one-sided (platform reference lanes: 2.6% of samples more than 5% above their row median, 0.17% more than 5% below) and min-then-subtract had the smallest error of the statistics compared on recorded samples. Every native aligner, API probe and untimed core executable runs after single-CPU pinning under a two-stage seccomp guard. Stage 1, installed before exec: any sched_setaffinity, clone, clone3, fork or vfork call terminates the process, non-x86_64 audit ABI and x32 calls terminate it, open/openat succeed only read-only (no O_WRONLY, O_RDWR, O_CREAT or O_TRUNC), and every syscall outside a short allow-list of memory, read, write-to-open-descriptor, clock and exit calls returns ENOSYS. Before dispatch, the trusted verifier checks every native candidate and reference executable for dynamic x86-64 ELF format and the system PT_INTERP loader; unsupported or static binaries invalidate the evaluation. Stage 2, installed by a preloaded judge library before main: stat-family calls and exec are denied as well. The process also has RLIMIT_FSIZE 0, /dev/null on stdin, an empty read-only working directory and a fixed four-variable environment. The policy denies file creation and modification, System V and POSIX IPC creation, memfd, sockets and signals. Read-only file access remains available for dynamic loading and input data; existing paths are not restricted to an input allow-list, and the guard does not guarantee isolation from every cross-execution observation. A self-test binary checks the listed operations on the actual runtime before any measurement; guard installation or self-test failure prevents execution. Fatal violations invalidate the whole evaluation without score or retry. No tolerance is introduced; the strict predicate is unchanged in form.
metrics.source: paper.txt, Section 3 and Table 1 (alignment-path run times); harbor/app/apps/aligner/aligner.cpp, main(): the -p and -l options select EDLIB_TASK_PATH and EDLIB_TASK_LOC for the same edlibAlign call; harbor/app/edlib/src/edlib.cpp, edlibAlign(): obtainAlignment is reached only under EDLIB_TASK_PATH. The fifteen-round interleaved protocol and the minimum are the task's declared measurement protocol, not a claim about the paper. Timed executions are validated by evaluator.py::checked_cli_run (parse_cli_run, replay) and evaluator.py::checked_location_run (parse_location_run); the statistic is evaluator.py::reconstruction_seconds; the comparison is evaluator.py::audit. The closure of the location-only mode is evaluator.py::check_surface / body_stays_in_function and evaluator.py::check_launch_surface / elf_surface.py. The guard is native_cmake.py::native_filter_instructions and judge/native_guard.c, proven per evaluation by evaluator.py::prepare_native_guard with judge/native_guard_selftest.c. Each duration is taken in native_cmake.py::run_bounded (pre-exec timestamp in the child, reap timestamp in the waiting thread).
metrics.clears_when: For each workload w: 0 < cpu_time_seconds_candidate(w) < cpu_time_seconds_reference(w), i.e. 0 < T_C(w) < T_R(w). Equality fails. A candidate difference that is zero or negative is not a measurement of a reconstruction and fails the workload; a workload whose reference difference is not positive cannot be passed. All fifteen path runs and fifteen location-only runs in each lane must complete successfully, print valid output for their mode and satisfy the validity requirements.

metrics.name: core_peak_live_bytes
metrics.means: For implementation X and workload w, A_X(w) = max over five fresh, untimed instrumented path-run processes of H + S + D, where H is the peak of requested live bytes obtained while the outermost obtainAlignmentHirschberg call is active (malloc, calloc, realloc, reallocarray, memalign, aligned_alloc, posix_memalign, valloc, pvalloc, and through them C++ new and allocations made inside libc and libstdc++ on the call's behalf, plus bytes mapped with mmap/mmap64; free and munmap of a whole mapping remove them), inclusive of recursive calls, transitively called native routines and returned alignment storage; S is the stack high-water mark of that call: the region below the core's own frame is painted at outermost entry and the lowest overwritten word is found at exit, measured from the core's frame address (the core is declared noinline in the derivative so the anchor is the same in both lanes); D is the total size of allocated writable or thread-local sections of the derivative's compiled edlib.cpp object (.data, .bss, .tdata, .tbss and any other section with SHF_ALLOC and SHF_WRITE or SHF_TLS), whether or not an input uses them. Pre-existing allocations, collector metadata and allocator overhead are excluded. Moving working storage between heap, stack and static storage therefore does not lower A. The collector defines the malloc family itself, so requests made inside libc are seen; references from the measured objects to __libc_malloc, __libc_calloc, __libc_realloc, __libc_memalign, __libc_free, mmap, mmap64 and munmap are redirected to it by the linker; mremap, sbrk, brk, shmat, dlopen, dlsym, dlvsym and the memory-obtaining numbers of the generic syscall() entry end the process (exit 86), as does a stack deeper than 4 MiB below the core frame, a core frame larger than 2 MiB, or a second outermost core entry in one process; each of these invalidates the evaluation. Exactly one evidence line per process is required. Each instrumented execution uses the path-run command line, runs under the same guard and has its printed path validated in the same way. Timing is measured on separate uninstrumented original builds.
metrics.source: core_measurement.py::build_core binds the exact submitted/restored source to private judge/core_alloc.cpp, marks the core noinline and inserts a trusted RAII entry/exit scope that passes the core's frame address; judge/core_alloc.cpp collects heap, mapped and stack bytes; core_measurement.py::static_bytes / elf_surface.py::static_storage_bytes read the static sections of the derivative's edlib.cpp object; core_measurement.py::parse_allocation and evaluator.py::_evaluate retain five samples and the maximum; evaluator.py::audit compares every row.
metrics.clears_when: For every workload w, core_peak_live_bytes_candidate(w) <= core_peak_live_bytes_reference(w), zero additional tolerance; equality passes. All five instrumented processes in both lanes must complete, enter the core exactly once and produce valid exact optimal paths. The strict reconstruction-time predicate 0 < T_C < T_R and all correctness gates are independently required.

beats_reference: Let W_train be all 30 frozen public performance workloads and W_final be all 60 frozen public and held-out performance workloads. For the evaluated split S, beats_reference(C,S) = 1 iff reference_qualification_complete AND measurement_complete(C,R,W_S) AND all_correctness_contracts_pass(C,S) AND (for every w in W_S: 0 < T_C(w) < T_R(w) AND A_C(w) <= A_R(w)), with T the reconstruction time (minimum path-run time minus minimum location-only time of one executable) and A the reconstruction storage (heap + stack + static) defined above. Otherwise it is 0; unavailable reference qualification must additionally be reported internally as unqualified, never as a completed scientific comparison. The predicate has exactly these two per-workload metrics. Process peak RSS is not part of it: wait4 ru_maxrss of the native process inherits the verifier process's own pre-exec high-water mark, so it does not measure the submission; it is still collected and reported privately for evidence. measurement_complete requires all fifteen fresh path runs, all fifteen fresh location-only runs and all five fresh instrumented runs of candidate and reference for every workload, valid positive durations, successful exits and no time or memory limit violation. all_correctness_contracts_pass includes every mandatory correctness case, the source and launch-surface checks, and validation of what every execution of the timed and instrumented executables prints on every performance input, including each timed sample of either mode. No omitted, failed, timed-out or unresolved workload can count as a pass, and no mean, geometric mean, weighted total, speedup average or ratio of aggregates enters this predicate. Continuous performance scoring is computed separately for valid submissions from the median path-run time and is never multiplied by, thresholded by or otherwise conditioned on this flag.

solver_feedback.name: candidate_diagnostic
solver_feedback.means: Present only when a development submission is rejected by a static check before any measurement (scored zero), in place of the measurements: one object from a fixed table with the category of the rejection (patch_policy, outside_before_body, outside_after_body, body_scope, body_forbidden_construct, launch_surface) and a fixed sentence saying the same; no number, path, symbol name, source text or workload identity.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no; a categorical fact about the candidate's own rejection built from a fixed table, without reference values, comparisons or identities; final responses never include it

statement_sentences: The strict comparison criterion has exactly two metrics, each decided on every workload after every correctness and execution gate passes. cpu_time_seconds: the reconstruction time, the smallest of fifteen verifier-measured path-run times minus the smallest of fifteen verifier-measured location-only times of the same executable on the same input, must be positive and strictly less than the reference's (zero tolerance; equality fails); the program's own printed time is only checked for consistency. core_peak_live_bytes: the storage of the reconstruction call, heap (requested live bytes including mapped memory) plus stack high-water plus static storage of the compiled source, measured by five separate untimed instrumented processes, no greater than reference (zero tolerance; equality passes); allocator overhead is excluded. No metric or row can compensate for another, and process resident memory (RSS) is not compared. Every execution, including each timed one of either kind, is validated before its time is accepted. No submitted code may run outside a call of the reconstruction function. The program runs under a restricted syscall policy that denies file creation and modification and the listed IPC operations while allowing read-only access to existing files. Train feedback is the continuous score and, per metric, the number of train workloads on which it clears, the number on which it does not and the total, with percentages (beat_spec_progress); reference values, ratios, individual workloads and per-workload measurements remain private.
comments: Train feedback is unchanged in kind: only beat_spec_progress (per metric passed/failed/total over the 30 train workloads, with percentages), keyed by the two metric names cpu_time_seconds and core_peak_live_bytes, which now carry the definitions above. solver_feedback names only candidate_diagnostic: a development submission rejected by a static check (patch policy, text outside the function body, the body leaving its function or using a screened construct, launch surface) returns a scored zero whose only metric is that fixed category and sentence (judge/candidate_failure.py, pinned by judge/candidate-diagnostic.json) in place of beat_spec_progress; it carries no reference-dependent bit. Outside the body the comparison with the pristine source ignores the number of blank lines, trailing spaces and tabs and CRLF against LF, and nothing else. Leakage bound (estimate): each train call returns two integers in 0..30 that depend on the reference, at most 2*log2(31) = 9.9 bits. A submission that recognises individual public inputs (forbidden by the statement) and sets its own per-workload time and storage could bisect per-workload reference values; storage is deterministic (about 17 bits per workload for an exact byte value) and time is noisy (about 5 bits per workload for a few percent). The 20 allowed train calls give at most about 200 bits against roughly 660 needed for all 60 values of the public suite, so they can locate some but not all of them; 100 calls would suffice. This is the channel every beat-spec task's per-metric counts expose; held-out workloads are never measured in train. While reference_qualification_complete is false every comparison is reported as not cleared. Current revision (2026-10-12, stronger reference): (a) the reference is no longer the restored upstream body; see upstream.lock.json source.stronger_reference for its provenance. (b) cpu_time_seconds is the reconstruction time, min(path runs) - min(location-only runs), fifteen interleaved rounds, instead of the median of five whole-process times: with the new reference the editable function is 0.5% to 15% of the whole-process time (median 5%) and the code placement of the unmodified search differs by about 5% between builds, so whole-process time no longer measured the reconstruction. (c) core_peak_live_bytes now counts heap (all malloc-family entry points and mmap), stack high-water and static storage; the previous definition counted malloc/calloc/realloc/new only and could be emptied by moving storage to the stack or to static arrays. (d) The body must stay inside its function and the built executable must have the reference build's launch surface, because the differential is only sound if no submitted code runs in the location-only mode. Workloads, seeds, the editable scope, the score formula's form, the guard and every limit are unchanged; the score now uses the median of fifteen path-run times. This revision has local evidence only: a same-version platform reference qualification has not been run. Known limits: a body that writes the rest of the program's output itself and ends the process (forbidden by the statement, and fatal in the instrumented runs unless the body also detects the derivative) removes the retained conversion and printing of the path from its own difference, which is 3% to 17% of the reference's difference on measured rows; storage obtained through a raw system-call instruction or through computed addresses of library routines is not attributed; the storage measurement runs on an instrumented derivative that a submission could in principle detect; a build's code placement can still affect the reconstruction code itself. Earlier history: Current revision (2026-10-12), three corrections with no change to the editable scope, workloads, seeds, sampling, the strict per-row elapsed-time rule, the heap metric's definition, the score formula or any limit. (1) peak_rss_bytes is removed from the comparison and kept as reported private evidence, because ru_maxrss inherits the verifier parent's high-water mark and the reference failed its own inequality on rows of its recorded qualification. (2) Timed executions now print the path (-p -f CIG_EXT instead of -p -s) and each of the five timed samples per lane is validated; previously the path was checked only in a separate invocation. The timed interval therefore additionally contains CIGAR conversion and buffered output, identically in both lanes; earlier samples are not directly comparable. (3) Native executables run under an allow-list seccomp guard with RLIMIT_FSIZE 0, piped output, a fixed environment and a read-only working directory, which deny the listed write and IPC operations without restricting all existing read-only paths; the previous guard only denied task creation and affinity changes. This revision has local reference-vs-reference evidence only: a same-version platform reference qualification has not been run. (4) The compared time is measured by the verifier around the whole process (pre-exec to reap) instead of being read from the program's own timer line, which a submission could forge by printing a complete output and exiting; the self-reported line is kept as a bounded diagnostic. The compared interval therefore also contains exec, loading, FASTA input and exit, the same fixed work in both lanes. Known limit that is unchanged: core_peak_live_bytes counts malloc-family requests only. History: Successor r005. Preserve every r004 row and original generator/seeds/indels/flanks; add70/80% strata at10k/30k in NW/SHW/HW, public+hidden, after authentic local30/60 fit succeeded (98.979181608s train,192.702331909s final). Five alternating fresh-process pairs and strict per-row CPU C<R unchanged. Peak RSS maximum5 C<=R zero tolerance is now independently graded, but inherited parent high-water contamination is measured: memory coverage is NOT qualified. No paper numerical RSS baseline or million-base scalability claim. Answering18000s,20traincalls,12000s trainpool,600s independentfinal unchanged. Aggregate per-metric feedback only; raw measurements/reference/rows private. Normal review/native reference/genuine/acceptance/audit pending; publishedr004 immutable. Current ONE strengthening round: allocation option A adopted. Publishedr004 and priorr005 evidence unchanged; no further hardening after valid solver results. Timing successor: process CPU API and nine-digit output only; no work count, boundary, sampling or acceptance change. Old clock()-based results are not directly comparable; same-version native qualification remains pending. Current successor: CLOCK_MONOTONIC at the same interval. CPU-to-elapsed semantic change; legacy identifiers retained. All metric predicates, resources, affinity, workloads, seeds and sampling unchanged. Diagnostic underreporting does not establish a 10 ms quantum. Old samples are not directly comparable; one new reference qualification is required after review and official publication. No retry-to-pass. Review requires fail-closed prevention of affinity widening and parallel worker creation before merge. The task-local native runner implements this with inherited seccomp rather than unreliable short-segment CPU/wall ratios. Only local validation is available; target runtime support and complete same-version reference qualification remain pending.
